title: Topic 8 · 情绪的建构 — 神经科学
title_en: Topic 8 · The Construction of Emotion — Neuroscience

questions.question: 按建构情绪论，同样是心跳加速，在悬崖边被感受成恐惧、在过山车上被感受成兴奋，主要差别来自哪里？
options: 大脑结合当下情境，用不同的情绪概念去解释同一份身体感觉
兴奋时主要分泌多巴胺，恐惧时主要分泌肾上腺素和皮质醇
两种场合下，杏仁核和自主神经系统的反应模式本来就完全不同
恐惧是进化预装的先天程序，兴奋则是后天在文化里学来的
questions.explanation: 建构论认为情绪是大脑用身体信号、学来的概念和情境当场拼出的解释：心跳一样快，标签一换，体验就变了。认为每种情绪各有专属的脑区、生理或化学「指纹」，正是被大样本汇总研究质疑的经典观。
questions.question_en: Under the theory of constructed emotion, a racing heart feels like fear at a cliff edge and thrill on a roller coaster. Where does the difference mainly come from?
options_en: The brain uses the situation to explain the same bodily state with different emotion concepts
Thrill mainly releases dopamine, while fear mainly releases adrenaline and cortisol
The amygdala and autonomic system respond in entirely different patterns in the two settings
Fear is an innate, prewired program, whereas thrill is learned later from culture
questions.explanation_en: Constructionism says an emotion is the brain's on-the-spot explanation built from body signals, learned concepts, and context: same heart rate, different label, different experience. The idea that each emotion has its own neural, physiological, or chemical fingerprint is the classical view that large meta-analyses call into question.

questions.question: 文章强调「核心情感本身还不是情绪」，这句话是什么意思？
options: 它是一阵情绪退去之后留下的长期心境，比单次的情绪更持久、也更稳定
它只是「舒不舒服、亢不亢奋」的身体底图，要套上概念才成为具体情绪
它就是少数几种进化预装、在各种文化里都相同的基本情绪
它只存在于还没有学会语言的婴儿和动物身上，成人已经没有
questions.explanation: 核心情感由效价和唤醒度两根轴组成，是一团尚未被命名的身体感觉；同一团「高唤醒、略不适」可以被建构成恐惧、兴奋或心动。把它等同于几种预装的基本情绪，等于又回到了文章要修正的经典观。
questions.question_en: The article stresses that 'core affect is not yet an emotion'. What does that mean?
options_en: It is the long-lasting mood left after an emotion fades, more stable than any single emotion
It is only a bodily map of pleasant-or-not and aroused-or-calm; a concept must be applied to make a specific emotion
It is the handful of prewired basic emotions that are the same in every culture
It exists only in infants and animals without language; adults no longer have it
questions.explanation_en: Core affect has two axes, valence and arousal, and is an as-yet-unnamed bodily feeling; the same 'high-arousal, slightly unpleasant' state can be built into fear, thrill, or a crush. Equating it with a few prewired basic emotions is the classical view the article sets out to revise.

questions.question: 按文章的解释，为什么情绪粒度高的人往往更善于调节情绪？
options: 先认准是哪一种情绪才能对症处理，而命名本身也在收束那团感受
他们的词汇量更大，向别人倾诉、求助时更容易得到理解
他们天生体验到的负面情绪就比较少，需要调节的场合也少
他们更擅长把情绪压下去，不让它在表情和行为上流露出来
questions.explanation: 粒度高意味着能把一团模糊的「难受」分辨成失望、焦虑或羞愧，分清了才知道下一步该做什么；而把弥散的核心情感收束成一个具体概念，本身就是一种调节，那股劲往往当场松一点。它靠的是辨认，不是压抑。
questions.question_en: According to the article, why are people with high emotional granularity usually better at regulating emotions?
options_en: You can only treat a feeling once you know which one it is, and naming it already helps contain it
Their larger vocabulary makes it easier to confide in others and be understood
They naturally feel fewer negative emotions, so there is less to regulate
They are better at suppressing feelings so nothing shows in their face or behavior
questions.explanation_en: High granularity lets you split a vague 'bad' into disappointment, anxiety, or shame, which tells you what to do next; and condensing diffuse core affect into a specific concept is itself a regulation move that often eases it on the spot. It works through recognition, not suppression.
